name: Jephthah's vow
charge: A rash vow, and its performance on his daughter
summary: Before battle with Ammon, Jephthah vowed that what came from his doors to meet him would be the Lord's. His only daughter came out with timbrels and dances. She accepted the dedication, mourned her virginity, and remained unmarried as her father fulfilled his vow.
offense: The vow itself was the sin: sworn thoughtlessly with the lips, as Leviticus describes, binding himself to a thing God never asked and, on the plain reading, forbade. Ecclesiastes: suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. The text records that she bewailed her virginity and knew no man; readers have long divided over whether the sacrifice was literal or a life devoted, and the text does not settle it.
judgment: He lost his only child and his line ended with him. The daughters of Israel kept a yearly lament for her. Jephthah is nonetheless counted among the faithful in Hebrews 11, which is the record's own tension.

entries.commentary: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah. His mother was a harlot, but he himself was a mighty man of valour. Gilead's wife's sons grew up and thrust out Jephthah: thou shalt not inherit in our father's house, for thou art the son of a strange woman. Strange woman here does not mean his mother was of another nation; the scripture says only that she was a harlot. His brothers cast him out of his father's house over his mother, though he had as much right to that house as they did. Jephthah fled from his brethren and dwelt in the land of Tob, and there were gathered vain men to Jephthah, and went out with him. Watch what that shows: when we do our brothers and sisters wrong, when the ones trying to do right do not get the love and support they need from their own family, they go looking for love in the wrong places, and you see the kind of men they gravitate to.

In process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel, and the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob: come and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon. Now they wanted the man of valour they had cast out. Jephthah answered, Did not ye hate me, and expel me out of my father's house? and why are ye come unto me now when ye are in distress? You hated me, you put me out, and now that trouble has come, you need me. He set the terms: if ye bring me home again to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD deliver them before me, shall I be your head? And the elders of Gilead said, The LORD be witness between us, if we do not so according to thy words; they called the Lord to judge them if they broke their word. Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and captain over them: and Jephthah uttered all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh.

Jephthah sent messengers unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land? He wanted to know what Ammon had against Israel. The king of Ammon answered, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and unto Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably. That claim was a lie, and Jephthah knew it.

Jephthah sent messengers again and broke down the whole history: Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon. He knew the record, so nobody could talk him out of it. When Israel came up from Egypt and walked through the wilderness unto the Red sea and came to Kadesh, they sent messengers to the king of Edom and to the king of Moab asking passage, and both refused; so Israel went along through the wilderness, compassed the land of Edom and the land of Moab, came by the east side of the land of Moab, and pitched on the other side of Arnon; but they came not within the border of Moab, for Arnon was the border of Moab. This is why we must know our history. The king of Ammon could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers.

So now the LORD God of Israel hath dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and shouldest thou possess it? The Lord moved the Amorites out by moving Israel in; why should Ammon possess what the Most High gave to Israel? Wilt not thou possess that which Chemosh thy god giveth thee? So whomsoever the LORD our God shall drive out from before us, them will we possess. You take what your god gives you; we will possess whatever the Most High gives us, and we are not backing down from anybody. Art thou any thing better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them? While Israel dwelt in Heshbon and her towns, and in Aroer and her towns, and in all the cities along the coasts of Arnon, three hundred years, why did ye not recover them within that time? Three hundred years Israel held that land and nobody came to claim it. Wherefore I have not sinned against thee, but thou doest me wrong to war against me: the LORD the Judge be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon. The Lord is in the midst of every battle; nothing goes down without the Most High letting it go down. World War One, the Lord was in the midst; World War Two, the Lord was in the midst; whoever he has destined to win is going to win. Howbeit the king of the children of Ammon hearkened not unto the words of Jephthah: the Lord had hardened their hearts not to listen, the same as he did with Sihon. The Most High strengthens nations and weakens nations, and moves peoples in and out of lands to fulfil his word. In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end; but if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen.

Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over unto the children of Ammon. Jephthah vowed a vow unto the LORD: if thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands, then whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace, shall surely be the LORD'S, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering. The vow was made before the battle, an offering promised to the Lord for the victory: whatever came out of his doors first would be given over to the Lord.

Jephthah passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hands. He smote them from Aroer even till thou come to Minnith, even twenty cities, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.

Jephthah came to Mizpeh unto his house, and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances; and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter. He rent his clothes and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low; for I have opened my mouth unto the LORD, and I cannot go back. A vow made to the Most High could not be taken back.

His daughter answered, My father, if thou hast opened thy mouth unto the LORD, do to me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth; forasmuch as the LORD hath taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon. She was not pleading for her life; she accepted that her life was now vowed to the Lord. She asked one thing: let me alone two months, that I may go up and down upon the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my fellows. To bewail is to weep and mourn; she went with her companions and mourned her virginity, because being given over to the Lord she would never know a man. Jephthah did not burn his daughter as a human sacrifice. Israel did not do human sacrifices; that was Molech worship among the Canaanites. Read the end of the passage: at the end of two months she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed, and she knew no man. If she had been put to death, there would be no reason for the scripture to say she knew no man; her life was committed to the Lord and she remained a virgin. Why would she mourn her virginity if she were about to die? Because the sorrow was that she could never marry or bear children. In those days our women wanted to bring children into the world and continue the lineage; to be without children was counted a shame and a dishonour among the daughters of Israel. A lot of people try to say Jephthah sacrificed his daughter, because our people do not understand the scriptures; keep reading and the text itself answers it. It is a translation difference around the word offering: she was presented to the Lord to serve him, not sent up as a burnt sacrifice. And it was a custom in Israel, that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

If a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it, if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity. Verse 4 defines the voice of swearing: a soul that swears, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good. If you know and say nothing, your brother's blood is required because you did nothing about it. We are to rebuke one another. Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil is a wicked saying; the scriptures say you renounce evil. The watchman does not cover his eyes, because he needs to see, and does not cover his mouth, because he gives the warning; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. If you do not apply this verse, you hate your brother in your heart; keeping quiet at his sin, or trimming your ways for him, is hate too. Stand still for the laws of the Most High and do not turn your ways for anybody, even carnal family that puts you out over your beard or your fringes. There is a way to correct: brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. A soft answer turneth away wrath; you do not render evil for evil and blast a brother, you build him up with a humble mind, and that is how souls are won. The man gathering sticks got the reproof that fit that willful case; meekness fits the brother overtaken in a fault.

Touching any unclean thing, the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man, leaves a soul unclean and guilty. This goes into eating, not mere contact; the classes have touched on this already, and it stands. It is the same as telling your son or daughter, get your hand out of the cookie jar: you say do not touch it, not do not eat it, because you know what the intention is. The Lord deals with us the same way; do not be touching that stuff means do not eat it, do not defile yourself. The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

If a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good, and it be hid from him, when he knoweth of it he is guilty. Brothers say, I swear to God; watch your mouth. When a man is guilty in one of these things, he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing, and bring his trespass offering, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin. A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

The offering scaled to what a man could bring: if he be not able to bring a lamb, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering; and if he be not able to bring those, the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour, with no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is a sin offering. The offerings were the collateral of those times, and families felt the after-effects of always sacrificing: the livestock and the agriculture went for your sins, and the household lacked because of it. Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent.

If a soul commit a trespass and sin through ignorance in the holy things of the Lord, he brings a ram without blemish, with thy estimation by shekels of silver after the shekel of the sanctuary; he makes amends for the harm done in the holy thing and adds the fifth part thereto for the priest, and it shall be forgiven him. The scripture that pops up again is the same one: if thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting; that card cannot be pulled on the Messiah.

If a soul sin against any of the commandments, though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity. Though he is ignorant of it, the iniquity is still there; saying I did not know does not remove sin, and everyone still appears before the judgment seat of Christ when it is all said and done. The priest made an atonement concerning his ignorance wherein he erred and wist it not, for he hath certainly trespassed against the Lord. The remedy is to know the law: let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments. The ordinances are found in the first five books; as these four chapters a day are conducted, meditate and study them continually. As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. The milk is the dos and the don'ts. Many want to run to Revelation and the parables, but the solutions for what is wrong in your spirit, for lust, covetousness, hatred, malice, and envy, sit in the ordinances and the commandments; look up the scriptures on patience, temperance, and how to treat your family correctly. Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth. A vow is promising the Lord you will do a thing. Say a man vows, Lord, if you bring this to pass I will never eat swine again; he must keep that vow, and he cannot go back on it and simply ask forgiveness afterward. If thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee; but that which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform. Do not suffer thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error.

A daughter in her father's house in her youth who vows a vow is under her father's covering. If her father hears her vow and holds his peace, all her vows stand and every bond wherewith she hath bound her soul stands. But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth, not any of her vows or bonds shall stand, and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her. That shows the power the Most High put in the man of the house: a father can hear his daughter bind herself and say no, and the Lord releases her.

The same covering passes to the husband. If a woman with a husband vows, or utters ought out of her lips wherewith she binds her soul, and her husband hears it and holds his peace in the day that he hears it, her vows stand. But if her husband disallow her on the day that he heard it, he makes her vow of none effect, and the Lord shall forgive her. A wife could be binding herself to something she cannot perform, and her husband can step in and say, Lord, do not hear that vow, and the Most High releases her because of her husband. That is the power of the head of the house: the husband keeping the commandments stands between his wife and a bond that would jack her up. That is a reason to love your hedge, not to despise it.

Every vow of a widow, and of her that is divorced, wherewith they have bound their souls, shall stand against her. She has no father or husband to disallow it, so what she vows she must perform. The husband is a hedge of protection; where no hedge is, the possession is spoiled. The married woman has a covering that the widow and the divorced woman do not have.

If a wife vowed in her husband's house and her husband heard it and held his peace and disallowed her not, then all her vows stand. Her husband may establish every vow and every binding oath to afflict the soul, or her husband may make it void. If he altogether holds his peace at her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows and confirms all her bonds, because he held his peace in the day that he heard them. Holding your peace is confirming it. But if he shall any ways make them void after that he hath heard them, then he shall bear her iniquity. He cannot hear her vow, hold his peace day after day, and then come later to void it; he had the power to stop it and did not, so the iniquity falls to him. And this runs one way: a wife cannot disallow or nullify her husband's vow. This is the order of the house: the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church, and he is the saviour of the body; so let the wives be subject to their own husbands in every thing, even in what is vowed in prayer.

These are the statutes which the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between the father and his daughter, being yet in her youth in her father's house. Keep your foot when you go to the house of the Most High and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they do not consider that they do evil. Be not rash with your mouth nor let your heart be hasty to utter anything before the Most High, for he is in heaven and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few. This means watch your mouth, which is why Christ said you will give account of every word. -

When you vow a vow to the Most High, do not defer to pay it, for he has no pleasure in fools; it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay. Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the angel that it was an error, lest the Most High be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands. This is what Christ meant by not swearing by heaven, earth, or your own head. -

If you see the oppression of the poor and the perverting of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel, for he that is higher than the highest regards it, and there are higher than they. Do not worry about the wicked that are successful and all they are doing, because there is a God and that God will have his vengeance. This is why the scriptures say vengeance is his and he will repay. -

He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he that loves abundance with increase; this also is vanity. When goods increase, those that eat them increase. As one rapper said, more money more problems: the more money most people get, the bigger their family gets, meaning the more food you can buy, the more mouths there are to feed. The sleep of a laboring man is sweet whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich will not let him sleep. The rich lose sleep to gain wealth; ask successful entrepreneurs and businessmen and they work off four or five hours of sleep.

There is a sore evil under the sun: riches kept for the owners to their hurt, and those riches perish by evil travail so that the son is left with nothing in his hand. As a man came from his mother's womb naked, so shall he return, and take nothing of his labor to carry away in his hand. In all points as he came, so shall he go, and he has labored for the wind, eating in darkness with much sorrow, wrath, and sickness.

It is good and comely for a man to eat, drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor all the days of his life which the Most High gives him, for it is his portion. Every man to whom the Most High gives riches, wealth, and power to enjoy them and rejoice in his labor, this is the gift of the Most High. He shall not much remember the days of his life, because the Most High answers him in the joy of his heart. Ecclesiastes is a book of regret, and we can learn from it; in the end you see what really matters in this life. Money is a defense, but keep the commandments in the faith of Christ, which is what Solomon was saying. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

These are the statutes and judgments which ye shall observe to do in the land: the Lord gave the fathers a land other nations were living in, and Israel went to war with those nations to take it. The whole book of Deuteronomy is the Lord speaking unto his people Israel; he showed his statutes and his judgments to no other nation.

Utterly destroy all the places wherein the nations served their gods, upon the high mountains, upon the hills, and under every green tree. Even after being warned, Israel was still idolatrous: the children of Israel secretly built high places in all their cities, set up images and groves in every high hill and under every green tree, and burnt incense as did the heathen, the very thing the Lord said ye shall not do. Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel; that is how they became the oppressor, and the word says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.
Unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there shall ye seek: out of all the tribes he chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and the temple.

Ye are not as yet come to the rest and to the inheritance: the rest is when the Lord gives rest from all your enemies round about, so that ye dwell in safety. This is why the scripture is pulled out on the street, this is not our rest: Israel today dwells among its enemies and serves them for food, shelter, and clothing, as [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) declares. Arise ye and depart does not mean to leave physically; it means come up out of the ways of this place, because it is polluted. Israel waits for the time when the third part has repented, the hundred forty and four thousand are sealed, and Christ returns to take his people out of this place and set them back in their own land.

Whatsoever thy soul lusteth after is not license to eat anything: it stays within the guidelines of the clean foods, as of the roebuck and as of the hart, the beasts listed in chapter 14, for the law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing. The unclean and the clean that may eat thereof are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats; Israel had servants then and will have servants again.

Take heed that thou be not snared by inquiring after the gods of the nations after they are destroyed, saying, how did these nations serve their gods, even so will I do likewise; Israel has a history of following what the other nations do. The snare fulfilled is written in the psalm: Israel did not destroy the nations, but was mingled among the heathen, learned their works, served their idols, and sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, the very abomination the Lord warned of here. The wrath of the Lord was kindled insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance; that snare is why Israel is where it is now, scattered among the heathen and serving them.

verses.text: And Jephthah vowed a vow unto the Lord, and said, If thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands,

Then it shall be, that whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall surely be the Lord’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.
And Jephthah came to Mizpeh unto his house, and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances: and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter.

And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he rent his clothes, and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou art one of them that trouble me: for I have opened my mouth unto the Lord, and I cannot go back.

And she said unto him, My father, if thou hast opened thy mouth unto the Lord, do to me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth; forasmuch as the Lord hath taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon.
And she said unto her father, Let this thing be done for me: let me alone two months, that I may go up and down upon the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my fellows.
And he said, Go. And he sent her away for two months: and she went with her companions, and bewailed her virginity upon the mountains.
And it came to pass at the end of two months, that she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed: and she knew no man. And it was a custom in Israel,
That the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

Or if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.
And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing:

And he shall bring his trespass offering unto the Lord for his sin which he hath sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin.
If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.
Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.
And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:

lawsResolved.text: If a person swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do evil or to do good, and whatever he pronounced by the oath is hidden or unknown to him, when he comes to know it, then he shall be guilty in these matters and shall confess them.
When you make a vow unto God, you shall not delay to pay it, for God will require you to keep your word.
We should avoid making any oaths so that you may not fall under judgment.
You shall not let any of your offspring pass through the fire of Molech.
Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry (be slow to anger).

text.text: And Jephthah vowed a vow unto the Lord, and said, If thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands,

Then it shall be, that whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall surely be the Lord’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.
And Jephthah came to Mizpeh unto his house, and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances: and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter.

And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he rent his clothes, and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou art one of them that trouble me: for I have opened my mouth unto the Lord, and I cannot go back.

And she said unto him, My father, if thou hast opened thy mouth unto the Lord, do to me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth; forasmuch as the Lord hath taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon.
And she said unto her father, Let this thing be done for me: let me alone two months, that I may go up and down upon the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my fellows.
And he said, Go. And he sent her away for two months: and she went with her companions, and bewailed her virginity upon the mountains.
And it came to pass at the end of two months, that she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed: and she knew no man. And it was a custom in Israel,
That the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

Or if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.
And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing:

And he shall bring his trespass offering unto the Lord for his sin which he hath sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin.
If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.
Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.
And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
